messages.author: 3d9e2c3d86fc8a6a
messages.subject: options for posterior marginals
parts:
Hello.  Havard, is it possible to specify the ranges or values the posterior marginals are evaluated at?  My posteriors are sometimes well away from zero at the boundaries.

p

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] options for posterior marginals
parts:
On Fri, 2011-06-10 at 07:52 -0700, Patrick Brown wrote:
> Hello. Havard, is it possible to specify the ranges or values the
> posterior marginals are evaluated at? My posteriors are sometimes
> well away from zero at the boundaries.
>
>
> p

yes, I have noticed that as well. this bound is in the c-code, as

#define GMRFLib_DENSITY_INTEGRATION_LIMIT (8.0)

which is 8 stdev in the *internal* scale. sometimes this is not
sufficient when transformed to the user scale...

I can change this to 10, say, and see if that helps ?

Another way out, is to use the marginals in the internal scale yourself
and extrapolate them when doing the transformation (inla.tmarginal). its
there as

> names(r$internal.marginals.hyperpar)
[1] "log precision for the gaussian observations"

and them smooth it with extrapolation, and then transform it,

> plot(inla.tmarginal(exp,
inla.smarginal(r
$internal.marginals.hyperpar[[1]], extrapolate=0.5)))


what you think? should we try a higher value ?

--
